title: Track what you have spent
prompt: Pocket has a `monthlyBudget` of 2000. Declare a variable `spent` that starts at `0`, then reassign it twice to add an expense of `45` and one of `120`. Declare `remaining` as `monthlyBudget` minus `spent`, and log the **type** of `remaining`. Keep `monthlyBudget` a `const`.
hints: `spent` has to change, so it cannot be a `const`.
To add to a variable, compute the new value from the old one: `spent = spent + 45;`.
`typeof` goes in front of the value: `console.log(typeof remaining);`.
explanation: `spent` is declared with `let` because it is pointed at a new number twice: `0`, then `45`, then `165`. Each time, the right side is evaluated using the current value before the name moves. `remaining` never changes after it is computed, so `const` is the right choice, and `typeof remaining` is `"number"` because subtracting two numbers gives a number. Trying to reassign `monthlyBudget` throws a `TypeError`, which is exactly the protection `const` is for.

checks.budget-const: `monthlyBudget` is still a `const` that cannot be reassigned
